title: Grateful Dead Live at Cleveland Music Hall on 1970-10-17
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) ->Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC/16

ai_review.summary: A decent audience tape captures a historic 1970 Cleveland show highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and strong first‑set jams.
ai_review.review: The recording, an audience (AUD) source from October 17 1970, is only fair in fidelity—there are noticeable cuts and the mix is thin—but it preserves a memorable performance. Highlights include a 19‑minute Dark Star, a fiery China > I Know You Rider segue, an inspired Other One and one of the best Good Lovin' renditions of the era, with Garcia’s guitar work especially praised. Despite the tape’s flaws, the band’s energy makes it a worthwhile listen for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the music (average show rating ~3.9) while noting consistent tape issues (average recording rating ~2.9). Weighted combination yields a solid 3.6‑star overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Decent for a 1970 audience tape; clarity is limited with several cuts (e.g., Truckin', Cold Rain & Snow) and occasional muffling, but Dark Star comes through relatively clean.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set launches strong with China>Rider and a fiery Other One, while the second set builds slowly before exploding into an extended Dark Star that carries the show’s momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia receives repeated praise for his soaring chords in Dark Star, sharp licks throughout, and a distinctive ascending riff noted by several reviewers.
band_member_comments.Phil: A rare bass solo is highlighted during Good Lovin', indicating Phil's standout contribution.
